articles.headline: Labour council launches White Ribbon film to help end violence against women
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has marked White Ribbon Day with a new film and social media clips, made with MAC Media Academy Cymru, to challenge harassment and abuse.
body: Swansea's Labour council has marked White Ribbon Day with a new short film and a set of social media clips, made with MAC Media Academy Cymru, to help stop violence against women and girls.

White Ribbon Day is also the International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women. White Ribbon UK's theme this year is It Takes All of Us: everyone has a part to play in challenging the attitudes and behaviour that can lead to violence against women and girls. To mark the day, the Guildhall was lit up orange.

The film and clips will be shared in communities across Swansea. They tackle harassment, catcalling and consent, and aim to get people talking about how each of us can help make our communities safer.
Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Swansea Labour is determined to end violence against women and girls."

The council says the day is a moment for all of us to think about what we can do at work, in public services and in our neighbourhoods. Labour wants every woman and girl in Swansea to feel safe, and this campaign shows a Labour council putting that priority into action.

articles.headline: Labour-backed Elysium transforms former JT Morgan building into gallery and cafe
articles.summary: Empty since 2008, the former JT Morgan building is open again as a gallery, cafe and artists' studios, in a project Swansea's Labour council has supported.
body: A city centre landmark that stood empty for years is open to the public again, after a project led by Elysium Gallery and Studios and supported by Swansea's Labour council transformed the former JT Morgan building.
Inside, there is now a gallery and a cafe, an education space, dozens of studios for artists, a quiet room and a function room that can be booked.

The building had been empty since 2008. Swansea's Labour council has supported the work through the UK Government's UK Shared Prosperity Fund, which helped pay for the internal works, the strip-out and improvements to the roof.

When the second phase of the work began last year, Labour council leader Cllr Rob Stewart said: "We're delighted to be supporting Elysium with their ongoing work to breathe new life into the former JT Morgan building as part of a project that will complement the fantastic cultural attractions Swansea already has, including our very own Glynn Vivian Art Gallery."
The gallery and cafe are open from 11am to 5pm, Wednesday to Saturday, so residents can call in and see the results for themselves.

Local Labour councillor for Castle, Cllr David Phillips, said: “So many people remember shopping in JT Morgan. Seeing the building full of life again, with a gallery and cafe open to everyone, is fantastic.”

Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Patience Bentu added: “This building sat empty for far too long. I would encourage everyone to pop in between Wednesday and Saturday and see what has been created.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Hannah Lawson added: “Dozens of artists now have studios right in the city centre. That creativity brings people into town and makes our streets more welcoming.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Fiona Gordon added: “Old buildings like this are part of Swansea's story. It is great that our Labour council has helped give this one a new chapter.”

Bringing much-loved old buildings back to life is a big part of Labour's plan for the city centre, alongside the new developments going up. It gives people more reasons to visit and keeps Swansea's history at the heart of the city.

articles.headline: Labour's Y Storfa hub welcomes more than 400,000 visitors in its first 11 months
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council opened Y Storfa to bring public services together in the city centre. Nearly a year on, more than 400,000 visitors have come through its doors.
body: Y Storfa, the city centre hub that Swansea's Labour council created to put key services under one roof, has welcomed more than 400,000 visitors in its first 11 months.
The hub on Oxford Street is open seven days a week, and on average more than 1,200 people a day now walk through its doors. It is getting ready to mark its first anniversary.

Residents can find Swansea Central Library, housing services, Careers Wales, Citizens Advice, West Glamorgan Archive Service, the South Wales Miners' Library and more in the same building. That means fewer trips across town and help that is easier to find.

Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Y Storfa is a fantastic facility, making services provided by us and others more accessible, while bringing significant new footfall to the city centre."

Partners in the building say the move is working. Caroline Newman, of Citizens Advice, said: "Our modern space has increased visibility and made it easier for residents to access advice." Students also use it as a calm place to study.

There is more to come. The council says plans for a coffee shop are progressing, and hospitality businesses interested in running a new city centre unit are invited to an informal face-to-face chat at Y Storfa, 277-278 Oxford Street, SA1 3EL, on Thursday 26 November from 2.30pm to 4.30pm.

Local Labour councillor for Castle, Cllr Patience Bentu, said: “Over 400,000 visits in under a year tells you how much people value having these services in one place. Y Storfa is a real asset for our city centre.”

Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Fiona Gordon added: “Whether you need the library, housing advice or Citizens Advice, you can now find it under one roof on Oxford Street. That makes a real difference to residents.”

Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Hannah Lawson added: “It is lovely to see Y Storfa so busy every day, with students, families and older residents all using it. Happy first birthday to a great community hub.”

Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr David Phillips added: “More than 1,200 visitors a day is good news for the shops and businesses around Oxford Street too. This is how we bring life back to the city centre.”
Y Storfa shows what Labour means by a city centre that works for local people: services that are easy to reach, and more footfall for the shops and businesses around them.

articles.headline: Labour urges residents to help shape one-ticket bus and rail travel for Swansea
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council wants one ticket to take you across a joined-up bus and rail network. Have your say on the Metro plans at drop-ins this week or online by 13 December.
body: Swansea's Labour council is backing plans for a joined-up bus and rail network where, in future, one ticket could take you to work, to school or on a day out across the city, and residents are being asked to help shape them.

Transport for Wales is consulting on plans to improve rail services as part of the Swansea Bay and West Wales Metro. Labour sees this as an important step towards Connect Swansea tickets and a network that is easy to use every day.

There are two drop-in sessions this week. The first is at Cockett Community Centre on Wednesday 25 November, from 2pm to 6pm. The second is at the Quadrant Shopping Centre on Thursday 26 November, from 9am to 5pm. If you cannot make either, you can take part online until 13 December.

Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Better transport connecting people with the place where they work, with schools and health services will help transform lives and the local economy.

"Our vision for a one ticket, one timetable on one network will mean we'll have a city where businesses can set up knowing they're within easy reach of their local workforce, creating jobs, investment and growth."

He added: "By getting involved, residents have the chance to help shape a vibrant future for our city where there's more well-paid jobs, a strong city centre and greater choice about what to do and where to go, thanks to a modern transport network that's everyday easy to use."

Local Labour councillor for Cockett, Cllr Mike Durke, said: “The drop-in is right here at Cockett Community Centre this afternoon, so please pop in. Your views will help shape how we get around Swansea for years to come.”

Fellow Cockett Labour councillor Cllr Elliott King added: “One ticket for buses and trains would make life easier for so many people in Cockett. Please take a few minutes to have your say before 13 December.”
Local Labour councillor for Castle, Cllr Fiona Gordon, said: “If you are in town on Thursday, call into the Quadrant and tell Transport for Wales what you need from public transport.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Patience Bentu added: “Good transport links are vital for the city centre. I would urge everyone to take part in the consultation.”

Labour wants public transport that fits around people's lives. Joined-up tickets and better rail links are part of building a city where good jobs, schools and health services are within easy reach for everyone.

articles.headline: Labour welcomes progress on Swansea cable car base station at Landore
articles.summary: The base station for Swansea's Kilvey Hill cable car is taking shape at Landore Park & Ride, and Labour council leader Cllr Rob Stewart has welcomed the progress.
body: The building where visitors will board Swansea's new cable car is now taking shape at Landore, and Labour council leader Cllr Rob Stewart has welcomed the latest progress.

Skyline, the company behind the project, says the main structure of the base station is continuing to rise beside the gondola tower at Landore Park & Ride. Once open, this will be where gondola journeys from the Copper Quarter to the top of Kilvey Hill begin.
Sharing the update, Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Great progress continues"

Local Labour councillor for Landore, Cllr Beverley Hopkins, said: “You can really see the base station building taking shape now at the Park & Ride. Residents have been watching it with real interest.”
Fellow Landore Labour councillor Cllr Mike White added: “Landore will be the starting point for every gondola journey. That puts our community right at the heart of this project.”

Earlier this month, Labour welcomed the first gondola tower going up at the foot of Kilvey Hill. Swansea's Labour council is backing projects like this because they bring visitors to the city and give local people something to be proud of.

articles.headline: Labour council seeks new members to help improve countryside access
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is re-forming the Swansea Local Access Forum and wants new members to help improve access to the countryside across Swansea and Gower.
body: Swansea's Labour council is inviting residents to help make the countryside of Swansea and Gower easier for everyone to enjoy, by joining the re-formed Swansea Local Access Forum.

The area has more than 400 miles of public paths and 26 square miles of access land, taking in some of Wales's finest coast and countryside. The forum's job is to advise the council, Natural Resources Wales and other bodies on how access to these places for open-air recreation can be improved.

Members discuss everything from walking and cycling to horse riding and other outdoor activities. The council wants a mix of people, including those who use the paths, landowners and land managers, and people with an interest in conservation or tourism. Members take part as individuals rather than on behalf of an organisation.
Anyone interested can find details of how to apply at swansea.gov.uk/localaccessforum. The deadline for applications is Friday 11 December 2026.
Labour wants Swansea's beaches, paths and open spaces to be open to all, and giving local people a say in how they are looked after is part of that.

articles.headline: Labour-backed sport and health institute reaches full height in Sketty
articles.summary: The National Institute for Sport and Health, backed by Swansea's Labour council, has been topped out on Sketty Lane. It opens next year and is set to bring skilled jobs to Swansea.
body: A major new centre for sport, health and skilled jobs is taking shape in Swansea with the backing of the city's Labour council. The National Institute for Sport and Health (NISH) on Sketty Lane has now been topped out.
Topping out means the building has reached its full height and its main structure is complete. It is a big step for a project that is due to open next year at the Swansea Bay Sports Park.

Once open, the institute will bring together experts in sport, health, science and technology. Their work will focus on new ideas, better health for local people and success in sport. It will also help local firms grow, draw in investment and create skilled jobs here in Swansea.

The council has congratulated Swansea University and everyone involved on reaching this point. Alongside the university, the project is backed by the Labour-run council, the Swansea Bay City Deal and other partners.
For Labour, this is what investing in Swansea's future looks like: world-class facilities, health research that can make a difference to people's lives, and good jobs for local people close to home.

articles.headline: Labour council looks for caring adults to help young people leaving care
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is looking for caring people to support young people leaving care through Shared Lives, helping them build life skills and confidence.
body: Swansea's Labour council wants to make sure no young person leaving care has to face adult life on their own. It is looking for caring, compassionate local people to give them steady support through Shared Lives.
Leaving care can be a daunting time. Many young people are still building their confidence while learning to manage adult life, and having a trusted adult alongside them can change a great deal.

Shared Lives gives care leavers the chance to learn practical skills for everyday life, grow in confidence and get consistent support as they move on. The people taking part offer guidance, encouragement and stability at a key moment.

The scheme is run as West Glamorgan Shared Lives, with Swansea Council and Neath Port Talbot Council. Anyone who thinks they could help can email westglamorgansharedlives@npt.gov.uk or call 01639 686123.

articles.headline: Thousands brave the rain as Labour council's Christmas Parade lights up Swansea
articles.summary: Thousands of people filled the city centre for the Christmas Parade put on by Swansea's Labour council. More than 40 local groups took part, and Santa switched on the lights.
body: Swansea's Labour council gave the city a bright start to Christmas on Sunday, when thousands of people filled the city centre streets for the annual Christmas Parade. It rained, and the crowds came anyway.

Local people were at the heart of it. More than 40 local groups joined the procession, among them Rising Stars Theatre Group, Loughor Town Band and Mellin Theatre Arts. Bonymaen Kids Play Initiative was there too, marking its 14th year in the parade.

Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Swansea truly came alive as thousands of people lined the streets for our spectacular Christmas Parade. It's one of the highlights of the festive calendar and I'm incredibly proud of the dedication, creativity and hard work that makes it such a success year after year."

The evening started at the Guildhall, where Santa turned the building a festive red and fireworks followed. There was entertainment on the Guildhall stage, which was supported by Specsavers (Swansea and Mumbles), before the award-winning parade set off.

Marching bands, festive characters and illuminated floats then made their way through the city. The Grinch and Witches of Oz floats were among the highlights, along with Spark! The Light Up Band, Winter Wonderland Birds and Space Cadets. The Land Rider had a seasonal makeover as well. With support from Childcare Offer for Wales, it became the Christmas Train.

There was live entertainment from Reagan Preece, a contestant on The Voice, from Victorian carollers and from the cast of Snow White at Swansea Grand Theatre. Santa finished the night by switching on the city centre Christmas lights and the Christmas tree, and a second fireworks display followed.

Cllr Stewart added: "It's a fantastic curtain-raiser to Christmas and an important boost for retailers, hospitality and other businesses at a vital time. Alongside free weekend buses, Winter Wonderland, the Christmas market and community Christmas parades, it demonstrates our commitment to supporting residents and businesses throughout the festive season."
Local Labour councillor for Castle, Cllr Patience Bentu, said: “What a night for our ward. Thousands of people came into the city centre in the rain, and the parade was worth every drop.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Fiona Gordon added: “More than 40 local groups took part, and that is what makes this parade special. Thank you to everyone who gave their time.”

Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Hannah Lawson added: “Seeing Santa switch on the city centre lights and the Christmas tree was a lovely start to the season. I hope families enjoyed it as much as I did.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr David Phillips added: “A busy city centre is good news for our shops, cafes and pubs. The parade brought people in at just the right time of year.”

A parade that fills the streets in the rain says a lot about Swansea, and about Labour's priorities. Labour wants a Christmas that families can enjoy together and that brings trade to local businesses when they need it most.

articles.headline: Labour council's Christmas Parade is this Sunday: what you need to know
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council starts the festive season this Sunday with the Christmas Parade. Santa leaves the Guildhall at 5pm, buses are free and there are quiet viewing areas.
body: Swansea's Labour council opens the festive season this Sunday, 22 November, with the city's Christmas Parade. Tens of thousands of people are expected, so here is what families need to know before they set off.

The fun begins before Santa appears. Entertainment starts at the Guildhall from 4pm and on the city centre stage from 4.15pm. Santa leaves the Guildhall at 5pm. The two entertainment stages are supported by Specsavers Swansea and Mumbles and will have live music, performances and family entertainment.

Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "The Swansea Christmas Parade is one of the highlights of the city's events calendar and it's fantastic to see so many community groups, performers and volunteers taking part, alongside a very special guest, Santa himself."

Getting there need not cost anything. The Labour council's free buses run all day on Sunday for journeys that start and finish within the Swansea Council area, and where services operate after 7pm they stay free until 9pm. Drivers can use extra parking at the Recreation Ground and Civic Centre West for £5 per vehicle. East Burrows and the usual city centre car parks are open too. The Fabian Way Park and Ride will not operate for this year's parade.
Cllr Stewart added: "The return of free bus travel makes it even easier for people to get to the parade, while additional parking will also be available."

The council has set aside space for people who need a calmer view. There are quiet and accessible viewing areas at the Guildhall and at the St Helen's Road end of The Kingsway, and nobody needs to book. Another quieter viewing area is halfway along St Helen's Road. The whole route will still have music, flashing lights and special effects.

Santa will have plenty of company: community groups, superheroes, colourful floats and characters from film and fairytale. This year's floats include the Grinch and the Witches of Oz, and there is a festive land train supported by the Childcare Offer for Wales. Festive lights and two fireworks displays add to the night.

Visitors are encouraged to arrive early and find a good spot. Christmas shopping, the Christmas markets and Winter Wonderland are all there to enjoy before the parade begins. Full details of the route, parking and travel are on the Visit Swansea Bay website.

A free parade, free buses to reach it and viewing areas for people who need a quieter space: this is Labour's approach to Christmas in Swansea. Labour wants every family to be able to join in, whatever their budget.

articles.headline: Labour council asks residents for their views, with £50 vouchers to be won
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council wants to hear from residents in its survey, Let's Talk: Living in Swansea. It closes on 6 December and there are £50 shopping vouchers to be won.
body: Swansea's Labour council is asking residents to say what they think about life in the city, and taking part brings the chance to win a £50 shopping voucher.

The council launched its latest appeal by answering a familiar complaint: that the city centre has no shops. Its reply is that the city centre has more than 200 retailers, an award-winning market, more than 150 hospitality businesses and 24 entertainment, culture and attraction venues. Now it wants residents to have their say.

The survey is called Let's Talk: Living in Swansea. It asks what is important to you, what your experience of your local area is, and how you view and deal with the council. It takes about 10 minutes and must be completed by 11.59pm on 6 December 2026.

Everyone who takes part can enter a free prize draw, with five £50 Love2Shop vouchers to be won. The survey is at swansea.gov.uk/residentssurvey, where Word and easy read versions are also available. The Welsh Local Government Association is running it on the council's behalf.
Decisions about Swansea to start with the people who live here. The more residents who reply, the clearer the picture the Labour council has of what matters in each community.

articles.headline: Labour welcomes new Men's Shed at Dyfatty Junction community hub
articles.summary: A new Men's Shed has launched at Dyfatty Junction, offering free weekly drop-in sessions. Swansea's Labour council is working with the project.
body: Men in Swansea who have been through probation, prison or substance services have a new place to find company and support, with the launch of a Men's Shed at Dyfatty Junction. Swansea's Labour council is working with the project and has shared news of the launch.

The Common Ground Shed meets every Tuesday from 2pm to 3pm. It gives men the chance to connect, chat and get support, and the sessions are run by mentors who have lived experience themselves. It is free and there is no need to book. Men can simply drop in.

Sessions are held at Dyfatty Junction, the community hub at the top of High Street. The hub opened in June, and Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, has said it is already proving a real success.

The new Shed joins a growing movement in the city. Earlier this month the Labour council awarded £40,000 to 23 Men's Sheds and similar community groups across Swansea, and it has invested £175,000 in Men's Sheds over the past seven years.
A friendly, free space for men who might otherwise struggle alone shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: stronger communities, second chances and support close to home.

articles.headline: Labour council buys former TSB building for new young people's hub on The Kingsway
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has bought the former TSB building on The Kingsway. It plans a major new city centre hub where young people and families can get support in one place.
body: Young people and families in Swansea are set to get a major new city centre hub, after the Labour council bought the former TSB building on The Kingsway.

The four-storey building at 29-30 The Kingsway is planned to house a range of services in one place. The aim is to make advice, guidance and support easier for young people to reach, in better surroundings.
Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Buying this building gives us a fantastic opportunity to create something really special for Swansea's young people.

"We want somewhere welcoming and accessible where young people can simply walk through the door, as well as a place where a wide range of organisations can work together to provide the support children, young people and families need.
"The former TSB building has huge potential and its city centre location means we can bring services that are currently spread across Swansea together in one place."

Under the plans, the council's Youth Justice Service would move in, together with the services now based at Info-Nation and young people's services that currently run from other sites in Swansea. The ambition is a welcoming "no wrong door" approach, so a young person can reach support from different services in one place.

The ground floor would be an open-access space for young people to drop in. Other floors could hold specialist services, rooms for consultation and assessment, family support and partner organisations. There is also scope for music and creative facilities, therapeutic support, space for workshops and training, and activities for health and wellbeing.

Cabinet members and the chairs of the relevant committees toured the building this week. The Labour administration will work with partners, including third-sector organisations, to draw up proposals for the hub and decide which services could move in. Cllr Stewart added: "We'll now continue working with young people, our partners and the third sector to help shape those plans."
Putting an empty city centre building back to work for the next generation shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: investing in young people, supporting families and making help easy to find.

articles.headline: Labour sets out 10-year vision for greener, safer parks across Swansea
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has approved a 10-year vision for its 149 parks, building on more than £11m already invested in play areas and skate and wheeled sports facilities.
body: Families across Swansea can look forward to parks that are greener, safer and more enjoyable to visit, under a new 10-year vision agreed by the city's Labour council.

Cabinet approved the Parks Development Strategy on November 18. It covers the 149 parks the council manages, from Singleton Park and Clyne Gardens to the green spaces in the middle of local communities. It builds on a strong record: more than £11m has already been invested in play areas and in skate and wheeled sports facilities.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Environment and Infrastructure, Cllr Andrew Stevens, said: "Parks can make a huge difference to everyday life. They give children somewhere to play, help people stay active, bring communities together and give all of us space to enjoy nature.
"We've already invested millions of pounds in improving facilities across Swansea, including our hugely-popular £8m play areas programme."

The strategy sets out opportunities for improved paths, lighting, seating and toilets, and for parks that are easier for everyone to get around. It wants parks to be more welcoming for teenagers, including spaces designed with teenage girls. Another key action is to use the National Exercise Referral Scheme to get more people active outdoors in parks and open spaces. Nature is central to the vision. It highlights tree planting, wildflower areas, better habitats and managing parks in a wildlife-friendly way, along with steps to help them deal with climate change and flooding. Communities would be encouraged to take a bigger part through park friends' groups, both existing and new.

Residents helped shape the plan. It was informed by 548 responses to a public survey, 27 stakeholder groups and 112 school pupils. Their priorities included maintenance, toilets, seating, accessibility, safety, facilities for teenagers and protecting nature.
Cllr Stevens added: "People have told us they want parks that are safer, greener, more accessible and welcoming to everybody.
"We want children growing up in Swansea today to inherit fantastic parks and, one day, be able to enjoy them with families of their own."

The improvements would be worked up as funding becomes available, so that investment is coordinated and goes where it will make the greatest difference. It shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: listening to residents, looking after nature and planning for the long term.

articles.headline: Labour's free buses are back this weekend: parade road closures to know
articles.summary: Labour's free buses return on 21 and 22 November for Swansea's Christmas Parade weekend. Here are the free bus dates and Sunday's road closures and parking restrictions.
body: Families can get into Swansea city centre by bus without paying a penny this weekend, thanks to Swansea's Labour council. Free buses are back on Saturday 21 and Sunday 22 November, just in time for the Christmas Parade.
The rules are the same as before: a journey is free if it starts and finishes within Swansea. On parade night, any services running after 7pm stay free until 9pm.

Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Swansea is the only council in Wales to offer this opportunity to take the bus and save money in the countdown to Christmas." He added: "Offering free buses to get to and from the Christmas parade is a brilliant early festive present for local families on what will be a great curtain-raiser for the countdown."

The parade is on Sunday 22 November. It starts at 5pm at the Guildhall and is expected to finish at about 6.30pm. The route runs along St Helen's Road and The Kingsway, then College Street, Castle Street and Caer Street, and ends on Princess Way. The city centre is expected to be very busy all afternoon, so allow plenty of time.

Some roads will be closed on Sunday. Guildhall Road North and Francis Street are closed from 8am to 10pm, and Bellevue Way from 12 noon to 9pm. Rolling closures apply from 4pm to 8pm on Guildhall Road South, St Helen's Road, St Helen's Crescent, Christina Street, The Kingsway, Orchard Street, Dillwyn Street, Castle Street, College Street, Caer Street, Castle Bailey Street, Princess Way, and Victoria Road and Oystermouth Road.

Parking is restricted too. From 8am to 10pm there is no parking on Guildhall Road North, Francis Street, the Guildhall Rotunda and The Baths car park. From 2pm to 8pm restrictions apply on St Helen's Road, St Helen's Crescent, The Kingsway, College Street, Castle Street and Princess Way. Drivers can park at the Recreation Ground to watch the start at the Guildhall, or avoid the closures completely by parking at the Civic Centre. A full list of city centre car parks is at swansea.gov.uk/carparks.

The free buses do not stop after the parade. They run again on 28 and 29 November, 5 and 6 December, 12 and 13 December, and 19 and 20 December. They then run every day from 21 to 31 December, when buses are operating. This is the sixth year in a row the Labour council has run the offer.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Community Support, Cllr Rebecca Fogarty, said: "Christmas can be an expensive time for everyone and a single family trip on free bus weekends can save them up to £20 in travel costs."

Local Labour councillor for Castle, Cllr Patience Bentu, said: “Free buses make it easier for families to come into the city centre and enjoy the parade. Please check the road closures before you set off on Sunday.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Fiona Gordon added: “A family can save up to £20 on a trip with the free buses. That is real help at an expensive time of year.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Hannah Lawson added: “The parade is one of the best nights of the year in our ward. Leave the car at home if you can and let the bus bring you in for free.”

Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr David Phillips added: “Our city centre shops, cafes and restaurants rely on a busy Christmas. Free buses every weekend until Christmas will bring them more customers.”

Free buses help families with the cost of Christmas and bring more customers to city centre shops, cafes and restaurants. That is Labour's priority for Swansea: practical help for residents and support for local businesses.

articles.headline: Labour backs 30 affordable homes at Swansea's historic Castle Cinema
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is helping to fund the restoration of the historic Castle Cinema building, which is being turned into 30 affordable homes, offices and a café or restaurant.
body: Thirty affordable homes are on the way in the heart of Swansea, as the Labour council backs the restoration of the city's historic Castle Cinema building.

Construction and restoration work is continuing at the building, which is being converted into 30 affordable apartments. There will also be small office units fronting The Strand, and a two-storey café or restaurant unit with a glazed box looking out over Worcester Place and Castle Square Gardens.
The scheme is led by Beacon Cymru Group and Easy Living Ltd. Swansea's Labour council is supporting it with funding, alongside the Welsh Government. The work is expected to be complete in 2028.

It sits next to another Labour project. Castle Square Gardens is also being redeveloped and is on course to open next summer. Laserzone, which used to be based in the cinema building, has moved to St David's Place.

Local Labour councillor for Castle, Cllr Patience Bentu, said: “Affordable homes in the city centre are badly needed. It is wonderful that 30 of them will be in a building so many people remember fondly.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Fiona Gordon added: “The old Castle Cinema is part of Swansea's story. I am glad to see it being restored and given a new use.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Hannah Lawson added: “Homes, offices and a new café or restaurant facing Castle Square Gardens will bring this corner of our ward back to life.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr David Phillips added: “More people living in the city centre is good for our shops and businesses. This scheme helps to make that happen.”
Bringing a historic building back into use, with homes people can afford, is what Labour wants for the city centre: heritage looked after and more people living at its heart.

articles.headline: Labour's Castle Square Gardens on course to open next summer
articles.summary: Swansea's new-look Castle Square Gardens is on target to open next summer. Labour council leader Cllr Rob Stewart visited the site this week to see the progress.
body: Swansea's new-look Castle Square Gardens is on course to open next summer, as Labour's transformation of the city centre square moves forward.
Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, went to the site this week with fellow cabinet members. They saw how far the work has come and heard the latest from main contractor Knights Brown.
Cllr Stewart said: "It's great to see the impressive progress being made. This is a complex project in a busy city-centre location, so I'm delighted it remains on target for opening next summer.
"The new-look Castle Square Gardens will create a fantastic space that people can enjoy for many years."

When it opens, the square will be a greener and more welcoming place in the heart of the city. It will have significantly more landscaping and new seating, with better facilities for events and for everyday use.

On site, drainage work has been carried out and the frames and roof structures are being built for the new commercial units. Each unit will have a green roof. The council is looking for ambitious café, restaurant and hospitality operators to move into them. Across the rest of the site, work continues towards new greenery, paving and granite planters.
Knights Brown said it was pleased with progress and was working closely with the council to deliver the project.
Residents can hear more at a community event on 26 November, from 2.30pm to 4.30pm, at Y Storfa on Oxford Street. The council's project team and Knights Brown will be there.

Local Labour councillor for Castle, Cllr Patience Bentu, said: “It is exciting to see the new Castle Square Gardens taking shape. A greener square with more seating will be a real asset for everyone who lives in and visits the city centre.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Fiona Gordon added: “New cafés and restaurants with green roofs will bring more life to the square. I am pleased the work is on target for next summer.”

Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Hannah Lawson added: “Building in the middle of a busy city centre is not easy, so it is good news that the project is still on course. I can't wait to see people enjoying the space.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr David Phillips added: “Castle Square is the heart of our ward. More landscaping and better facilities for events are just what it needs.”
Castle Square is part of the Labour council's £1bn regeneration programme. It shows what Labour wants for Swansea: a city centre with more green space, more life and more reasons to visit.

body: The first gondola tower for Swansea's new cable car is now standing at the base of Kilvey Hill, and Labour council leader Cllr Rob Stewart has welcomed the progress.

Labour is backing projects like this because they bring visitors to Swansea, create new opportunities and give the city something to be proud of.

articles.headline: Labour council confirms free Wales Airshow returns on 24 and 25 July 2027
articles.summary: Wales' largest free event is coming back. Swansea's Labour council has confirmed the Wales Airshow will return on 24 and 25 July 2027, with an invite going to the Red Arrows.
body: Wales' largest free event is coming back. Swansea's Labour council has confirmed that the Wales Airshow will return to Swansea on 24 and 25 July 2027.
The award-winning show draws more than 200,000 visitors each year, with families and aviation fans travelling from across the UK.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Development, Cllr Andrew Williams, said: "We are delighted to confirm the return of the Wales Airshow in 2027. It's a major feature of the summer season and brings thousands of visitors to Swansea each year."

Over the two days, a variety of aircraft will fly displays above the five-mile sweep of Swansea Bay. On the ground there will be fairground rides, live music, exhibitors, family entertainment, and food and drink.

The last show ended with Afterburn, an evening programme of flying displays, a display by two hundred drones celebrating Welsh culture, and a fireworks finale. The Labour council is now looking at bringing it back.

Cllr Williams said: "Our teams are already working on their plans for next year and that includes looking at proposals for a return of the hugely successful Afterburn show. And, of course, an there will be an invite to the Red Arrows after they missed last year due to commitments in the United States.
"We know how much the Red Arrows love the Swansea crowds, so we're hopeful we'll be on their list when they reveal their plans next year."
The full flying programme and more entertainment will be announced nearer the time. Updates will be posted at www.walesairshow.com and by @walesairshow on Facebook and Instagram.
A free event on this scale brings visitors and trade to the city, and gives local families a great weekend out. Labour is keeping it at the heart of Swansea's summer.

articles.headline: Labour council lines up weeks of festive family fun for Swansea city centre
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is bringing weeks of Christmas events to the city centre, from Winter Wonderland on 19 November to the Fire & Ice Festival on 5 December, with free festive buses too.
body: Swansea's Labour council has lined up a packed Christmas programme for the city centre, giving families somewhere to go and something to do from this week right through the festive season.
It starts on 19 November, when Winter Wonderland opens at Museum Green. Visitors can skate on the ice, ride the big wheel and the fairground rides, and stop for food and drink.

The city centre's Christmas Market follows on 21 November. The Christmas Parade and Lights Switch On come a day later, on 22 November. Mistletoe & Markets is on 28 November, and the Fire & Ice Festival is back on 5 December.

Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Christmas is always a special time in Swansea and we want families to have plenty of reasons to come to the city centre and enjoy everything on offer."

There is plenty indoors too, with festive activities for families at cultural attractions such as the Grand Theatre and Glynn Vivian. The Labour council also wants the season to be a good one for local traders. Shops, independent businesses, Swansea Market stallholders, cafés, restaurants and entertainment venues are all ready to welcome visitors.

Getting there will cost less as well, because free bus travel will be on offer at points over the festive period. Labour's free buses run on 21 and 22 November for the parade weekend, on every weekend in the countdown to Christmas, and from 21 to 31 December when buses are operating. More details are at www.visitswanseabay.com.

A busy, welcoming city centre at Christmas is good for families and good for the businesses that depend on it. Labour is making sure Swansea has both, with events for all ages and help with the cost of getting there.

articles.headline: St Helen's hosts first international since Labour council-backed redevelopment
articles.summary: International rugby has been played at St Helen's for the first time since the redevelopment supported by Swansea's Labour council, with Wales U19s beating France U19s 34 - 31.
body: Swansea rugby fans have watched international rugby at St Helen's for the first time since the historic ground's redevelopment, a project supported by Swansea's Labour council.

Wales U19s took on France U19s there on the evening of Saturday November 14, and staged a comeback to win 34 - 31. It gave supporters the chance to see the international stars of the future on their doorstep.
The redevelopment has given St Helen's a new role as the home of the Ospreys, Swansea RFC and community sport.

Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: “This is another exciting milestone in the ongoing redevelopment of St Helen’s, which demonstrates the progress being made in securing a bright future for this famous ground. It’s also great to see the Welsh Rugby Union showing confidence in St Helen’s as a venue for international sport.
“We’ve already seen how successfully St Helen’s has embraced its new role as the home of the Ospreys, alongside Swansea RFC and community sport, bringing new energy and excitement to the venue.

“Hosting fixtures like this reinforces our ambition to make St Helen’s a thriving home for rugby at every level, from grassroots and community participation through to the professional and international game.”

Backing a famous ground so it can serve everyone, from local clubs to international sides, shows where Labour's priorities lie: investing in the places Swansea is proud of and making sure communities share in the benefit.

articles.headline: Labour council starts Killay flood scheme: what the traffic changes mean
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is moving ahead with its major scheme to protect Killay from flooding. Traffic around Killay Square changes from Monday 16 November.
body: Killay is getting better protection from flooding in severe rainfall, as Swansea's Labour council moves ahead with a major scheme at Killay Square. Drivers will see changes to traffic in the area from Monday 16 November.

From that date, vehicles will not be able to get onto Gower Road from Goetre Fawr Road. Goetre Fawr Road will become one-way between Gower Road and Broadmead, with traffic heading towards Dunvant Road.

Drivers coming from Gowerton or Dunvant to the shops in Killay should use Dunvant Road and Goetre Fach Road. Through traffic should carry on along Dunvant Road and Wimmerfield Drive to reach Sketty or Gower.
The work is expected to take around 25 weeks. Anyone who regularly travels through Killay is asked to allow a little extra time for their journey.

The Labour administration is installing an 'overflow' drainage system at Killay Square, because the existing drains cannot cope with the volume of water in heavy rain. Flooding has repeatedly forced the junction to close. The scheme is funded through the Welsh Government Regional Transport Fund.
Residents who want to know more can call in at Killay Library, where there is more information and a public display about the scheme.

Local Labour councillor for Dunvant & Killay, Cllr Louise Gibbard, said: “We all know what happens at Killay Square when the heavy rain comes, so it is good to see this work under way. Please allow a little extra time for your journey while it is done.”

A few months of changed routes will leave Killay with a junction that stays open when the weather turns. That is Labour's priority for Swansea: fixing long-standing local problems properly, and being straight with residents about what the work involves.

body: Shoppers and visitors can now use the Copr Bay North car park in Swansea city centre, and new digital screens on its side are telling people what is coming up in the city. Swansea's Labour council has shared the latest progress.

There is good news on the shops too. The council says talks are progressing well with a number of retailers who are interested in taking on the retail units below the car park.

articles.headline: Labour council brings Pension Credit help to Gorseinon with free drop-in session
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is helping older residents in Gorseinon check if they can claim Pension Credit, at a drop-in session on 19 November.
body: Older people in Gorseinon can find out whether they are missing out on Pension Credit, thanks to a drop-in session supported by Swansea's Labour council on 19 November.
The session runs from 9.30am to 12.30pm at Maes Yr Efail, West Street, Gorseinon, SA4 4AE. It is the first in a series of drop-ins the council is supporting over the coming weeks.
Anyone over State Pension age may be eligible to claim. The council's Financial Inclusion Team can help people check what they are entitled to.

A successful claim can unlock much more than the payment itself. It could bring free dental care, free or discounted eye tests and glasses, a Council Tax reduction and help with rent. It can also give access to Winter Fuel Vouchers and the Warm Home Discount Scheme, and a free TV Licence for people over 75.

Local Labour councillor for Gorseinon & Penyrheol, Cllr Andrew Stevens, said: “Too many pensioners miss out on money that is theirs by right. If you or someone you know might qualify, please call in at Maes Yr Efail on 19 November.”

Fellow Gorseinon & Penyrheol Labour councillor Cllr Jan Curtice added: “I am really pleased this session is coming to Gorseinon. Pension Credit can open the door to help with dental care, eye tests and Council Tax, so it is well worth checking.”

Fellow Gorseinon & Penyrheol Labour councillor Cllr Nicola Matthews added: “A quick chat with the Financial Inclusion Team could make a real difference this winter. Please tell older friends, family and neighbours about it.”

Labour councillors want every pensioner to receive the support they are due. Taking this help into the heart of the community is typical of the Labour administration's priorities: putting money back in people's pockets and looking after those who need it most this winter.

articles.headline: Labour invites residents to see progress on new-look Castle Square Gardens
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is inviting residents to meet the Castle Square Gardens project team and contractors Knights Brown at Y Storfa on 26 November.
body: People in Swansea can find out for themselves how the new-look Castle Square Gardens is coming along, at a community engagement event organised by Swansea's Labour council.

The event takes place on 26 November, from 2.30pm to 4.30pm, at Y Storfa, 277-278 Oxford Street, SA1 3EL. Members of the council's project team will be there, along with main contractors Knights Brown, to meet residents and talk about the work.
This will not be the only chance to hear about the scheme. The council says more community engagement events will follow.

Castle Square Gardens is part of the Labour administration's wider investment in Swansea city centre. Once the work is complete, more than 40% of the square will be green space. There will be extra trees and planting, interactive water features, better public spaces, and new places to eat and drink in café and restaurant pavilions. The scheme is due to open in summer 2027.
Work on site has been moving on. In September the council said the steelwork was complete for one of the new pavilion buildings.
Speaking in September, Labour Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "People can already see that Castle Square Gardens is starting to take shape."

Local Labour councillor for Castle, Cllr Patience Bentu, said: “Castle Square is right at the heart of our ward, so I'd encourage residents to call in at Y Storfa, meet the team and ask their questions.”

Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Fiona Gordon added: “More than 40% of the new square will be green space. That is a big change for the city centre, and I'm glad people are being invited in to see how it is going.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Hannah Lawson added: “It's good that the project team and the contractors are making time to talk to local people. I hope lots of our residents can come along.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr David Phillips added: “I'm looking forward to the new trees, planting and water features in Castle Square. This event is a good chance to hear what happens next.”

Labour wants a greener, more welcoming city centre, and wants residents to be part of it as it takes shape. Opening the doors so people can meet the team and ask questions shows the Labour council's priority: building the city centre with the people who use it.

articles.headline: Labour council to host new team for North Gate Swansea's £20m Pride in Place programme
articles.summary: Three new staff will help turn community ideas into action in North Gate Swansea's £20 million Pride in Place programme. Swansea's Labour council will host the team.
body: Communities from Upper High Street to Hafod are getting a dedicated team to help turn local ideas into action. Three people have been appointed to deliver North Gate Swansea's £20 million Pride in Place programme, and Swansea's Labour council will host them.
Alfie joins as full-time Programme Lead, Dawn as full-time Programme Officer and Helen as part-time Programme Officer. They were chosen from 74 applications after a competitive recruitment process.

The programme provides £20 million over 10 years for lasting improvements across Upper High Street, Dyfatty, Hafod, Waun Wen, Brynmelyn, North Hill and surrounding neighbourhoods inside its boundary. It is funded by the UK Government and is designed so that local people are central to decisions about where they live.

The Labour-run council is the programme's accountable body. The staff will take their direction from the Independent Chair, Thom Lynch, and the Neighbourhood Board. Their posts are paid for from the programme's early capacity funding, so the board has dedicated support while it carries on developing its priorities and long-term investment plans.

The new team will begin work on 30 November and 7 December 2026. Their first task is to get out and meet residents, businesses, charities, schools and community organisations. They will also go through the feedback and ideas already collected.

Between them, the three bring experience in project management, community development, youth work, grant management, and supporting children, families and vulnerable people. They have worked in communities across Swansea, including in the North Gate area.
Residents can have their say through the programme's community survey, join its mailing list at northgateswanseapip.co.uk/contact, or email hello@northgateswanseapip.co.uk.

Local Labour councillor for Castle, Cllr Patience Bentu, said: “People in Dyfatty, Waun Wen and around High Street have plenty of ideas for their area. A team on the ground will help turn those ideas into action.”
Fellow Castle Labour councillor Cllr Fiona Gordon added: “I'm pleased the council is hosting this team. I'd urge everyone in the North Gate area to fill in the community survey and have their say.”

Local Labour councillor for Landore, Cllr Beverley Hopkins, said: “This is welcome news for Hafod. £20 million over 10 years is a real chance for local people to shape lasting improvements where they live.”
Fellow Landore Labour councillor Cllr Mike White added: “A warm welcome to Alfie, Dawn and Helen. I look forward to them meeting residents and groups in Hafod when they start work.”

Labour believes the people who live in a neighbourhood know best what it needs. By hosting this team, the Labour council is helping North Gate's communities shape £20 million of investment over the next 10 years.

Local Labour councillor for Waunarlwydd, Cllr Wendy Lewis, said: “Victoria Road is used by so many of us in Waunarlwydd, so a full resurfacing is very welcome. Thank you to residents for their patience during the evening closures.”
Good local roads matter to every community. A full resurfacing of a village road like this one shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: investing in the basics and looking after every neighbourhood.

articles.headline: Labour councillors bring Morriston's Christmas parade and lights switch-on back
articles.summary: Morriston's Christmas parade and lights switch-on returns on Friday 27 November from 5pm, organised and funded by the ward's Labour councillors.
body: Families in Morriston can look forward to a free night of festive fun this month, as the ward's Labour councillors bring back the Christmas parade and Christmas lights switch-on.
The Great Morriston Christmas Lights Switch On 2026 takes place on Friday 27 November. The fun starts at 5pm, and the lights will be switched on at 6pm when Santa arrives in his sleigh.
The annual event is organised and funded by Morriston's Labour councillors. It is one of the highlights of the year for the community and brings people of all ages into the heart of Morriston.
Nation Radio's Big Breakfast presenter Phil Hoyles will host the evening. There will also be a very special guest appearance by Morriston's own Regan Preece, from The Voice.
The evening opens at 5pm with performances by local school and adult choirs. There will be a parade and a Christmas tree switch-on, and fireworks will follow the big switch-on.
The event is supported by Swansea Council and by local sponsors Day's, Castle and Peter Lynn & Partners.
Labour councillors in Morriston are asking residents to share the word and come along.
Local Labour councillor for Morriston, Cllr Andrea Harrington, said: “The lights switch-on is one of my favourite nights of the year in Morriston. Come along from 5pm and bring the whole family.”
Labour candidate for Morriston, Andrew Francis-Davies, added: “Our local choirs open the evening and they are always wonderful. I hope to see lots of you there to cheer them on.”

Local Labour councillor for Morriston, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: “Seeing the children's faces when Santa arrives in his sleigh makes all the planning worth it. Please share the word with your neighbours.”
Fellow Morriston Labour councillor Cllr Yvonne Jardine added: “We are proud to bring this event back for our community, and it is lovely to have Morriston's own Regan Preece joining us this year.”

Fellow Morriston Labour councillor Cllr Rebecca Francis-Davies added: “It's brilliant to see our Labour councillors bringing the Christmas parade and lights switch-on back to Morriston. Make sure you stay for the fireworks after the big switch-on.”

Labour believes that every community in Swansea deserves events that bring people together. Morriston's Labour councillors organise this night each year because they want local families to enjoy Christmas close to home.

articles.headline: Labour takes new 350-place special school a major step forward
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has submitted a full planning application for a new Ysgol Calon Lân, a purpose-built special school for up to 350 learners with 100 extra places.
body: Children and young people with additional learning needs in Swansea are a step closer to a new purpose-built school. Swansea's Labour council has submitted a full planning application for the new Ysgol Calon Lân.

The proposed school at Mynydd Garnllwyd Road would be a centre of excellence for up to 350 children and young people. It will replace Ysgol Calon Lân's existing three sites and create an additional 100 places, so more learners can get the specialist support they need within the Swansea Council area.

Labour's Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "Submitting the planning application is another major milestone in our plans to deliver a fantastic new school for Swansea. This is a hugely important investment in our children and young people and our ambition is to create an outstanding environment where every learner has the opportunity to thrive."

The plans include a swimming and hydrotherapy pool, specialist health and therapy spaces, sensory and quiet rooms, rebound and soft-play areas, specialist classrooms and spaces supporting independent living skills. Outside, pupils would have dedicated play and learning areas, sports facilities, a forest school and chances to learn and spend time in nature.

A separate six-bedroom 24-hour curriculum unit would offer overnight stays and help young people develop independent living skills. The school would be on a single storey, designed to support transition around the building, with direct access from classrooms to outdoor areas. Separate drop-off areas for different groups of learners are also proposed.

School governors, staff, pupils and families have helped shape the design. Labour's Cabinet Member for Education, Cllr Robert Smith, said: "The people who know Ysgol Calon Lân best have helped shape these plans, including pupils, families, staff and governors. That input has been invaluable. The result is a school designed around its learners, with first-class specialist facilities alongside welcoming classrooms and fantastic outdoor spaces."

The Labour-run council is developing the school with contractor Morgan Sindall and consultants WSP. It will be part funded by the Welsh Government. The planning application will now be considered through the council's usual planning process.

Local Labour councillor for Mynyddbach, Cllr Mike Lewis, said: “A new purpose-built Ysgol Calon Lân at Mynydd Garnllwyd Road would be a wonderful thing for our community. I am pleased to see the plans reach this stage.”

Fellow Mynyddbach Labour councillor Cllr Sam Pritchard added: “Pupils, families, staff and governors have helped shape this school, and it shows. A hydrotherapy pool, sensory rooms and a forest school would make a real difference to learners.”

Fellow Mynyddbach Labour councillor Cllr Jess Pritchard added: “An extra 100 places means more children can get specialist support close to home. I look forward to following the plans as they go through the planning process.”

Labour believes every child in Swansea deserves a school built around their needs. This investment shows that the learners who need the most support are at the heart of Labour's plans for education in the city.

articles.headline: Labour congratulates Ysgol Gymraeg Tan-y-lan on gold careers award
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has congratulated Ysgol Gymraeg Tan-y-lan on winning the Gold Award at the Careers Wales Quality Awards, with Ysgol Uwchradd Bryntawe taking Silver.
body: Pupils at a Swansea Welsh-medium school are getting some of the best careers education in Wales, and Swansea's Labour council has congratulated them on a national award that proves it.
Ysgol Gymraeg Tan-y-lan has won the Gold Award at the Careers Wales Quality Awards. The school was also runner-up for the Outstanding Careers Leadership Award for schools across Wales.

The Labour-run council said the award was brilliant recognition for the pupils and staff who work hard to make careers education an important part of school life. That work helps young people discover opportunities, explore their ambitions and prepare for their futures.

Headteacher Berian Jones said: "I could not be prouder of our school community. These awards recognise the ambition, teamwork and shared belief in helping every child reach their full potential. Special recognition also goes to Careers and RVE Co-ordinator Mrs Davies for her leadership and dedication."
There was more good news for Welsh-medium education in the city. Ysgol Uwchradd Bryntawe also had reason to celebrate after winning the Silver Award.
Labour's Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, shared the news and the council's congratulations with residents.

Local Labour councillor for Mynyddbach, Cllr Mike Lewis, said: “Huge congratulations to everyone at Ysgol Gymraeg Tan-y-lan. A Gold Award is a fantastic achievement and our community is very proud of the pupils and staff.”

Fellow Mynyddbach Labour councillor Cllr Sam Pritchard added: “Helping children think about their futures from a young age really matters. Well done to Mr Jones, Mrs Davies and the whole school on this recognition.”

Fellow Mynyddbach Labour councillor Cllr Jess Pritchard added: “Gold at the Careers Wales Quality Awards and runner-up for careers leadership across Wales. Llongyfarchiadau to all at Tan-y-lan, you have earned it.”

Labour wants every child in Swansea to leave school with ambition and a clear idea of where they can go next. Two Swansea schools being recognised at national level shows what pupils and staff can achieve, and Labour will keep backing them.

articles.headline: Labour council opens online evening for anyone thinking of fostering
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is making it easier to find out about fostering, with a Foster Wales Swansea online information session on Thursday 19 November, 6pm to 7pm.
body: Swansea's Labour council is making it easier for people to find out whether fostering is right for them, with an online information evening they can join from home.
Foster Wales Swansea is hosting the session on Thursday 19 November, from 6pm to 7pm. It is aimed at anyone who cannot get to an in-person event.
People joining will be able to meet members of the fostering team and some of Swansea's foster carers. The carers will share their experiences, answer questions and explain what fostering involves.

The Labour-run council said that deciding whether to foster is a big step, and the choice needs to feel right for everyone in the household. That applies whether you are single, married, have children, work full time or have pets.
The evening is designed to be relaxed, with time to find out about fostering, listen to foster carers and ask questions.

Anyone who cannot make the date still has options. Foster Wales Swansea regularly holds information stands across the city, so there is always a chance to speak to the team close to home. Details are on the Foster Wales Swansea Facebook page and at www.swansea.fosterwales.gov.wales.

Making it simple to ask questions, without pressure and without leaving the house, shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: backing foster carers and helping more local people consider opening their homes to children who need them.

articles.headline: Labour council's sold-out fireworks spectacular charms thousands at Singleton Park
articles.summary: Thousands packed Singleton Park for a sold-out myths and magic fireworks night put on by Swansea's Labour council, the show's first year at its new home.
body: Thousands of Swansea families enjoyed a sold-out night of magic, fire and fireworks at Singleton Park, as the city's much-loved fireworks show made its debut at the new home chosen by Swansea's Labour council.

This year's event had a myths and magic theme. The Labour administration brought the show to the park with support from the Childcare Offer for Wales, and a specially created interactive story turned Singleton Park into a world of fantasy, mixing magic, mystery, comedy and plenty of audience participation.
A Fairy Godmother and a host of magical characters led the crowd through the evening. Thousands of spectators joined mass dances, cast spells and helped good triumph over dark magic.

Families watched performances from Mellin Theatre Arts and Heather Dolly Jones, and a magical spell revealed a giant 7ft animatronics dragon. A fire performance followed, before a spectacular fireworks and laser display lit up the Swansea sky to close the night.
Labour's Leader of Swansea Council, Cllr Rob Stewart, said: "It was fantastic to see so many people come together to enjoy what was a truly magical evening at Singleton Park.

"The event showcased everything that makes Swansea's events programme so special, bringing communities together in a safe, welcoming environment and creating memorable experiences for families and friends."
The fireworks night is part of an autumn events programme put on by Labour councillors, which continues with the Swansea Christmas Parade on November 22 and Swansea Winter Wonderland.
A safe, affordable night out that thousands of families could share in one of the city's best-loved parks: that is what Labour's priorities for Swansea look like in practice.

articles.headline: Labour council closes two more illegal vape shops in Swansea
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has shut two more St Helen's Road shops caught selling illegal vapes and counterfeit tobacco, taking the total closed since June to 14.
body: Swansea's Labour council has closed two more shops that were selling illegal vapes and counterfeit tobacco, protecting residents and local high streets from dangerous goods.
Kubas Superstore and Swansea Market Vape Store, both on St Helen's Road in the city centre, have been ordered by Magistrates to close for three months. They cannot trade during that time.
The closures follow visits by the council's Trading Standards team. Test purchases made before those visits found the shops were still selling counterfeit tobacco and illegal vape products.

Both shops had already been closed by Trading Standards once before. Under current law, a three-month closure order is the longest penalty magistrates can give. Two men connected to the Swansea Market store were also recently jailed for a total of five years.
The action takes the number of vape shops closed by the Labour administration since June this year to 14, with some closed more than once.
Labour's Cabinet Member for Development - Control, Cllr Andrew Williams, said: "The latest closures are part of our ongoing campaign against illegal vape sales in the city.
"We've closed a total of 14 vape shops since June this year, following investigations by our Trading Standards. Some we have closed more than once.

"Current legislation means that we can only close these shops for a period of three months at a time. I want to reassure the public that we will continue revisiting these premises when they reopen and take action to close them down again if they are caught selling illegal vapes. Our aim is to disrupt this illegal trade that is impacting our high streets."

Going back to the same shops again and again, and closing them every time they break the law, shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: safe high streets, protection for residents and children, and a fair deal for the honest traders who play by the rules.

articles.headline: Labour council's £40,000 boost for 23 Men's Sheds across Swansea
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has awarded £40,000 to 23 Sheds across the city, helping people connect, learn new skills and beat loneliness. It takes Labour's investment in Men's Sheds to £175,000 over seven years.
body: Hundreds of people who rely on Men's Sheds and similar community groups across Swansea are set to benefit from a £40,000 funding boost from Swansea's Labour council. The money has been awarded to 23 Sheds across the city, helping them keep providing places where people can connect, learn new skills and improve their wellbeing.

The grants will pay for activities, equipment, training and essential running costs, so groups can keep their doors open and create welcoming Sheds where people socialise, share interests and reduce isolation.

This latest round builds on the Labour administration's long-standing support for the movement. Over the past seven years, Swansea Council has invested £175,000 in Men's Sheds, helping the number of Sheds across the city grow significantly and enabling hundreds of people to benefit from their activities.

Among the successful applicants is Llansamlet Men's Shed, where the funding will help members develop new practical skills through woodworking and support its growing ukulele group, which aims to perform in local halls and residential homes.

The Ivy's Men's and Women's Shed will use its grant to run a programme of workshops covering a range of crafts and practical skills. The project will also provide opportunities for younger adults with learning disabilities through a local partnership, and help meet the running costs that keep the Shed operating.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Community Support, Cllr Rebecca Fogarty, said: "Men's Sheds and similar community groups play an important role in helping people stay connected, active and involved in their local communities.
"This funding will help groups continue providing welcoming spaces where people can learn new skills, build confidence, make new friendships and support one another.

"We've seen first-hand the positive difference these groups make in tackling loneliness and improving wellbeing. We're proud to have invested £175,000 in Men's Sheds in recent years and I'm delighted we'll be supporting 23 projects through this latest round of funding."

Local Labour councillor for Llansamlet, Cllr Ryland Doyle, said: “Llansamlet Men's Shed is a lifeline for people who might otherwise be on their own. I'm delighted this funding will support its woodworking and the ukulele group.”

Fellow Llansamlet Labour councillor Cllr Matthew Jones added: “This grant from our Labour council will help keep Llansamlet Men's Shed's doors open, paying for activities, equipment, training and the everyday running costs. It's a real boost for our community.”

Fellow Llansamlet Labour councillor Cllr Penny Matthews added: “Learning a new skill alongside friends does wonders for people's confidence and wellbeing. Our Labour council's support for Llansamlet Men's Shed is money well spent.”

Fellow Llansamlet Labour councillor Cllr Alyson Anthony added: “Tackling loneliness matters in every part of Llansamlet. Sheds like ours bring people together, and £175,000 over seven years shows how seriously Labour takes that.”

Backing 23 Sheds with grants that cover the basics as well as new activities shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: strong communities, support for the volunteers who run them, and practical help for people who might otherwise feel alone.

articles.headline: Labour council replaces Uplands traffic lights as part of £14m roads investment
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council has started replacing the old traffic lights at the main Uplands junction, part of its £14 million investment in roads and highways for 2026/27. Temporary lights run from 9 November.
body: Drivers, bus passengers and pedestrians in Uplands are getting new traffic lights at the area's main junction. Swansea's Labour council has started work to replace the old signals where Gwydr Square meets Uplands Crescent.

The scheme is part of the Labour administration's £14 million investment in roads and highways infrastructure across Swansea for 2026/27, the same programme that is resurfacing roads and filling potholes in every part of the city.

From 9 November, temporary traffic lights will control the junction for a few weeks while the new lights are installed. The council says it will do everything it can to keep traffic flowing as normal, but drivers may experience some delays while the work is completed.

Anyone travelling through Uplands over the coming weeks may want to allow a little extra time. Once the work is finished, the junction will have modern signals in place of the worn-out ones that have served the area until now.

Replacing old traffic lights is not glamorous, but it is the kind of everyday work that keeps Swansea moving safely. Labour councillors pushed for this year's record roads budget so that junctions, pavements and road surfaces across the city get the attention they need.
This shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: investing in the basics, looking after every neighbourhood, and keeping residents informed when work affects their journeys.

articles.headline: Labour council's £76,000 green energy boost for rural Swansea groups
articles.summary: Swansea's Labour council is giving five rural community organisations more than £76,000 for solar panels, batteries, heat pumps and EV chargers, cutting their energy bills for good.
body: Five community organisations across rural Swansea are getting more than £76,000 from Swansea's Labour council to cut their energy bills, reduce carbon emissions and make their buildings more sustainable. The money means more can be spent on the activities and services residents rely on.

The Labour administration awarded the funding through the UK Local Growth Fund Rural Renewable Energy Grant Programme. It will pay for renewable energy improvements at vital community facilities in Loughor, Pontarddulais, Clydach and Three Crosses.
Loughor RFC 1882 has received £24,216 for solar panels and battery storage at its clubhouse, which also hosts community groups, veterans and a weekly foodbank.

Bont Elim Community Church in Pontarddulais has secured £15,916 for additional heat pumps, while Clydach Community Council will receive £14,749 for solar panels and battery storage at Forge Fach Resource Centre.

Three Crosses Community Council has been awarded £8,369 for electric vehicle charging points and battery storage. The 4th Lliw Valley Scout Group will also benefit from £13,382 for solar panels, battery storage and LED lighting.

Labour's Cabinet Member for Environment and Infrastructure, Cllr Andrew Stevens, said: "By helping organisations cut their energy bills, we're making sure more money can go towards the activities and services that really matter to residents."
Further funding remains available for eligible rural community organisations. Groups can find out more by emailing ruralanchor@swansea.gov.uk.

Local Labour councillor for Llwchwr, Cllr Adam Davis, said: “Loughor RFC is far more than a rugby club. Its clubhouse hosts community groups, veterans and a weekly foodbank, so solar panels and battery storage there will help a lot of people.”

Fellow Llwchwr Labour councillor Cllr Kelly Roberts added: “I'm delighted that £24,216 is going to Loughor RFC 1882 to cut its energy bills. Every pound saved on electricity is a pound that can go back into the community.”

Local Labour councillor for Pontarddulais, Cllr Philip Downing, said: “Bont Elim Community Church and the 4th Lliw Valley Scout Group do wonderful work in Pontarddulais. Heat pumps, solar panels and LED lighting will make their buildings cheaper to run for years to come.”

From scout halls to rugby clubs and community centres, this investment shows Labour's priorities for Swansea: backing the volunteers who hold rural communities together, cutting running costs for good causes, and protecting the environment at the same time.

articles.headline: Labour council lands Becky Hill as first headliner for Tunes on the Bay 2027
articles.summary: BRIT Award winner Becky Hill will headline Friday 30 April 2027 on Swansea Bay Beach as Labour's council brings Tunes on the Bay back for a third year.
body: Swansea's Labour council is bringing one of the UK's biggest dance-pop names to the city's beach. BRIT Award-winning Becky Hill has been announced as the Friday headline artist for Tunes on the Bay 2027, giving residents a major live music event on their doorstep.
She will take to the stage on Swansea Bay Beach on Friday 30 April 2027, as the three-day music festival returns for its third year under the Labour administration.

Hill first came to national attention on The Voice UK and went on to achieve her first UK number one with the Oliver Heldens collaboration Gecko (Overdrive). She has since won the BRIT Award for Best Dance Act twice, in 2022 and 2023.
Her hits include Remember, Heaven on My Mind, My Heart Goes (La Di Da), Disconnect and Crazy What Love Can Do, and she has collaborated with David Guetta, Ella Henderson, Chase & Status and Sigala.

Her headline appearance will kick-start the third Tunes on the Bay. Saturday already boasts a line-up of dance, hard dance and drum and bass talent, including Billy Gillies, Lisa Lashes, General Levy, Eddie Halliwell, Tidy Boys, DJ Hazard, FISH56OCTAGON, Alex Kidd, DJ Hype, Judge Jules and more.
Labour's Cabinet Member for Development, Cllr Andrew Williams, said: "It's fantastic to see an artist of Becky Hill's calibre announced as the opening headliner for next year's Tunes on the Bay.
"Events like this bring thousands of people to Swansea and give visitors another reason to spend time in the city, while showcasing the incredible setting we have here on Swansea Bay.

"With a number of exciting events and live music already taking shape, 2027 is looking set to be a very promising year for music in Swansea. This announcement is a great way to start building that excitement, and I'm sure there'll be plenty of anticipation around what else is still to come."

Tickets for Becky Hill at Tunes on the Bay are now on sale, and further artists will be announced in the coming weeks. Tickets and information are at www.visitswanseabay.com. Big events on the bay show Labour's priorities for Swansea: a city with more to do, more visitors spending in local businesses, and a reputation as a place worth coming to.
